sections.text:
Extractability in **GEO (Generative Engine Optimization)** is the degree to which your content can be cleanly *pulled out, understood, and reused* by AI answer engines as standalone, citation‑ready snippets.[1][2][4]

In the context of GEO (not “geographical” or “gene expression omnibus” GEO), **extractability** specifically means:

- **AI can identify and understand your key claims**  
  It is “the degree to which AI systems can identify, understand, pull, and reuse useful information from your content.”[1]

- **Chunks work as standalone answer blocks**  
  Extractable content is written so its key claims “can be pulled out of context and still make sense.”[4]  
  Large language models and answer engines ingest pages as *chunks*, not full linear articles; they “retrieve chunks, evaluate them in isolation, and synthesize answers from the fragments” that pass relevance and trust checks.[4]

- **Answer‑first, self‑contained formatting**  
  GEO audits describe extractability as checking “whether a clean, useful answer can be pulled from your pages without an AI system having to dig through paragraphs of vague marketing copy.”[2]  
  Practical guidance includes:
  - Put a **direct answer in the first ~80–150 words** of the page so AI doesn’t have to infer it from long setup text.[2][4]  
  - Use **literal, descriptive headings** and **semantic HTML** so answer engines can map sections to specific questions.[2]  
  - Create **self‑contained answer blocks** where each paragraph clearly answers a question, names the relevant entity, and points to evidence.[4]

- **Clear entities and attribution**  
  A GEO audit looks at whether your site provides “clear, verifiable, and extractable data” about what your brand is, who it serves, and why it should be trusted.[2]  
  Extractable blocks should:
  - name the **entity and category** (e.g., “X is a cybersecurity platform for financial institutions”),[4]  
  - attach **sources to claims** in proximity to the sentences they support,[4]  
  - avoid pronoun‑heavy wording that becomes unclear when a single sentence is isolated.[4]

- **Why it matters in GEO**  
  Generative Engine Optimization “focuses on being included in generated answers,” and “extractable content is easier to retrieve, synthesize, and cite,” making extractability “a core part of GEO.”[1]  
  GEO practitioners explicitly treat extractability as one of the main pillars alongside entity clarity and proof: a GEO audit “evaluates entity clarity, answer extractability, and brand proof to secure citations in AI‑generated answers.”[2]  

If you’re optimizing for GEO, you can think of **extractability** as:  
> *Can an AI system copy one paragraph from this page and have it still answer a specific question, name the right entity, and be safe to cite?*  
If yes, that paragraph—and by extension your page—is extractable.[1][4]
